_: THE OFFICIAL-ACTIVITY CODEBOOK. One definition, read by Python (ETL/events/transform/classify_taxonomy.py) and TypeScript (web/scripts/check_sector_evidence.ts). A second copy would be the bug, not the safeguard.
_property: sector_top is a claim about what a company's core business BUILDS. Only evidence about the company's own activity licenses it; a grant is evidence about the PROGRAMME, never about its recipient. The official registered activity descriptor outranks anything we derived (Rule Zero), so where EVERY official descriptor NAMES an activity with no technology, science or engineering dimension, no technology sector may be claimed.
_matching: Fragments are matched case-insensitively as substrings of a registered activity descriptor, in EXACTLY this order: `unspecific` first (a descriptor that names no activity can neither license nor veto), then `licenses_technology` (a descriptor that names a technology activity settles it), then `nontech`. Both languages must apply all three steps; applying only `nontech` reads NACE section R -- 'HUMAN HEALTH AND SOCIAL WORK ACTIVITIES', the section that contains hospitals -- as an activity with no science in it.
_boundaries: ASYMMETRIC: a veto refuses a technology claim, it never re-assigns one to a different technology sector.
A code must NAME an activity to veto one. Residual and holding registrations name none.
SILENCE IS NOT A VETO: an unrecognised descriptor is not evidence that a company sits outside technology.
licenses_technology: manufacture of medical and dental instruments
research and experimental development on biotechnology
unspecific: other professional, scientific and technical activities
